decision: Alicia Dietz Studios describes a free first consultation held virtually, followed by a design fee for three concepts, review of design choices and a later contract and production schedule. That published sequence supports a more useful website brief than a portfolio alone. Imagine a customer wanting a console for a narrow entry, with a place for keys and charging cables. The first discussion establishes the use and style; paid design development explores possible solutions. The website should make that transition visible before the customer schedules, and explain how choices in design, materials or detail affect the proposal. I can clarify an existing consultation page or build a portfolio that follows an example through those stages. The maker confirms the actual terms, dimensions and final design.

pages: Paid design stage and later agreement
scopes.request: Describe the piece’s use and space, understand the first meeting, then decide whether to proceed under the maker’s design-development terms.
scopes.supplies: Current consultation arrangements, the exact transition to paid work, design deliverables and what requires later agreement.
scopes.check: The narrow-entry customer can prepare a useful first discussion and understand the design fee before proceeding; booking the free meeting does not read as a promise of free design concepts.

scopes.title: Build a commission portfolio that explains decisions
scopes.request: Follow an approved example from the original need through design alternatives to the agreed commission, then start a discussion about a new piece.
scopes.supplies: Permissioned images or renderings, the maker’s accurate contribution at each stage, actual revision/approval terms and current scheduling language.
scopes.check: An example labels a concept rendering separately from the finished piece. A visitor can see why a design choice changed the proposal and knows that choosing a concept alone does not reserve a production slot.

scopeTrigger: A focused edit fits when good work examples already exist and the free-to-paid transition is unclear. A fuller build fits when visitors need to see how the brief becomes concepts and an agreed piece. Interactive design tools, customer portals or custom payment integrations require separate website/software scope. Furniture design, fabrication specifications, commission terms and production scheduling remain with the maker.
